cases.n: Fr Nicolás Aguilar Rivera — Puebla diocese priest in Los Angeles
cases.victims_note: 26 grade-school children per a 1988 police report
cases.who: Archdiocese of Los Angeles; Diocese of Tehuacán (Mexico)
cases.cover: Plaintiffs' attorneys produced a 1988 letter from the Bishop of Tehuacán saying he had warned Cardinal Mahony in 1987 about the priest; the archdiocese denied receiving the warning. The priest fled to Mexico after being relieved of duties and was never arrested.
cases.d: A visiting Mexican priest was assigned to two Los Angeles parishes in 1987. A 1988 police report says he abused 26 grade-school children between March 1987 and January 1988, many recruited as altar servers. A parent reported abuse to a pastor on 8 January 1988; he was removed the next day, charged with 19 felony counts of lewd acts on a child, but fled to Mexico before arrest. As of 2004 the case remained open.
cases.cite: Associated Press, 'Attorneys: Mahony ignored warnings from Mexican bishop', 30 April 2004 (via BishopAccountability.org)

cases.n: Fr Joseph Jeyapaul — Indian priest extradited to Minnesota
cases.who: Diocese of Crookston, Minnesota; diocese in India
cases.cover: The Vatican recommended his removal from the priesthood, but the Indian bishop instead imposed a year in a monastery through a canonical trial, and he continued as a priest in India.
cases.d: An Indian priest serving in the Diocese of Crookston in 2004–2005 was removed from ministry in September 2005 and returned to India. He was charged in 2006 with raping a girl from age 14; extradition took about five years after an Interpol alert, with arrest in Erode, India in 2012 and return to Minnesota in November 2014. In 2015 he pleaded guilty to criminal sexual misconduct involving a teenage girl and was sentenced to a year and a day (time served); the rape charges were dismissed under the plea deal and he faced deportation to India.
cases.cite: MPR News, 17 Nov 2014; Star Tribune, 15 June 2015

cases.n: Joseph Henn — Salvatorian priest, fugitive in Rome, extradited 2019
cases.who: Society of the Divine Saviour (Salvatorians); Diocese of Phoenix
cases.cover: After his 2003 indictment he fled to Italy; Italy's top court confirmed extradition after his 2005 arrest there, but he disappeared before it could be carried out, remaining a fugitive until May 2019.
cases.d: Henn served at St Mark Parish in Phoenix from 1978 to 1982 and was accused of molesting at least three boys under 15 between 1979 and 1981. Maricopa County indicted him on 13 child-molestation counts in 2003. He was expelled from his order and removed from the priesthood in 2006. Italian police arrested him in Rome on 28 May 2019; U.S. marshals returned him and he was arraigned in Phoenix on 14 June 2019.
cases.cite: Catholic News Service / National Catholic Reporter, 17 June 2019

cases.n: Fr Johannes Rivoire — Oblate in Nunavut, never extradited from France
cases.place: Arviat, Rankin Inlet, Naujaat and Whale Cove, Nunavut
cases.victims_note: review found on the balance of evidence that he assaulted six children, plus evidence of another victim c.1968–70
cases.who: Oblates of Mary Immaculate (OMI Lacombe Canada; Oblates of France)
cases.cover: He left for France in January 1993; a Canadian arrest warrant followed in 1998 and charges were later stayed. A 2022 warrant led to an extradition request that French authorities denied. The 2024 Denis review found the RCMP never contacted the Oblates when charges were laid. In February 2024 the Vatican ruled against his dismissal. He died in France in 2024 without trial.
cases.d: French Oblate Johannes Rivoire worked in the Canadian North from 1959 to 1993. He faced at least three sexual-abuse charges (1998 warrant) concerning Inuit children in Arviat, Rankin Inlet and Naujaat, and a 2022 warrant for indecent assault on a girl in Arviat and Whale Cove between 1974 and 1979. A March 2024 review by retired Quebec justice André Denis, commissioned by the Oblates, concluded on the preponderance of evidence that he assaulted six children. Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami called his death without trial in April 2024 'a systemic failure of nation states and religious institutions'.
cases.cite: Canadian Press via Global News, 19 March 2024; Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami statement, 12 April 2024

cases.n: Colombia — Constitutional Court orders Medellín archdiocese to release priests' files
cases.who: Archdiocese of Medellín; Salesian Inspectorate of San Luis Beltrán, Medellín
cases.cover: Both the archdiocese and the Salesian province refused journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos's 2019 request for the records of 43 priests, calling them private; the archdiocese appealed the first-instance ruling against it.
cases.d: In May 2019 journalist Juan Pablo Barrientos, author of 'Dejad que los niños vengan a mí', asked the Archdiocese of Medellín and the Salesians for the records of 43 priests, including complaints against them. After both refused, he filed tutela actions. On 3 March 2020 the Constitutional Court ruled that the information was semi-private and that the right to information prevailed, ordering the archdiocese to hand it over. In 2022 the Court agreed to review a further petition covering 915 priests who served in Medellín.
cases.cite: El Espectador, 3 March 2020; Infobae, 2 Feb 2022

cases.n: Ecuador — Fr César Cordero Moscoso, Cuenca
cases.who: Archdiocese of Cuenca; schools founded by Cordero; Catholic University of Cuenca
cases.cover: First accusations date from 2010, but he remained honoured; the case drew attention only in 2018 when the Cuenca city council planned to decorate him.
cases.d: Cordero Moscoso founded the Catholic University of Cuenca and led it from 1970 to 2013. In 2018 five men reported he had abused them as children at a school he founded. The Archdiocese of Cuenca accepted their testimonies as credible and apologised, and after a report sent to Pope Francis the Vatican dismissed him permanently from the clerical state in October 2018. His statue and decorations were removed. He died in 2023 aged 95 without a criminal conviction.
cases.cite: El Universo, 4 Oct 2018; Primicias, 4 Feb 2023

cases.n: Ecuador — 103 complaints of sexual violence against clergy (Ecuavisa)
cases.victims_note: 103 complaints; the outlet calls it an undercount
cases.who: Catholic clergy in Ecuador
cases.cover: Victims' families said the church hierarchy refused to share information or file complaints with prosecutors itself, contrary to a National Assembly commission report on sexual violence against children in education.
cases.d: A months-long investigation by Ecuavisa's Visión 360 counted 103 complaints of sexual abuse involving Ecuadorian clergy, with cases in Guayas, Pichincha, Azuay and Los Ríos, including those of Fr César Cordero and Fr Luis Intriago. A survivors' association demanded that such crimes be made imprescriptible, as approved in a referendum.
cases.cite: El Oriente (Ecuador), reporting Ecuavisa Visión 360

cases.n: Paraguay — Fr Carlos Urrutigoity and the removal of Bishop Livieres
cases.who: Diocese of Ciudad del Este
cases.cover: After accusations in the US (a 2002 complaint over students at St Gregory's Academy in the Diocese of Scranton), he moved with his group to Ciudad del Este, where Bishop Rogelio Livieres made him vicar general in 2014. Pope Francis removed Livieres in 2014; Urrutigoity left in June 2015. La Nación reported at least five Argentine priests accused of abuse or crimes against humanity had sheltered in Paraguay.
cases.d: Argentine priest Carlos Urrutigoity was accused in 2002 in the US of sleeping with boarding-school students, giving them alcohol and sexually abusing a recently graduated seminarian. He then moved to the Diocese of Ciudad del Este, Paraguay, and became its second-in-command in 2014. His case reportedly cost Bishop Livieres his post when Pope Francis removed him in 2014. He was moved back to Mendoza, Argentina, in June 2015. He has not been convicted.
cases.cite: La Nación (Paraguay), 23 May 2016

cases.n: Costa Rica — Fr Mauricio Víquez, convicted after fleeing to Mexico
cases.who: Archdiocese of San José; Episcopal Conference of Costa Rica
cases.cover: A San José civil court ordered Archbishop José Rafael Quirós, the Episcopal Conference and the church's property entity to pay 65 million colones; the victims' lawyer said the church knew from 2002 and did nothing. Three other complaints were declared time-barred.
cases.d: Víquez, a former church spokesman on family issues, fled Costa Rica in 2018 when accusations surfaced, going via Panama to San Nicolás de los Garza, Mexico, where he was caught; he was extradited in 2021. The church expelled him from the clergy in 2019. In March 2022 he was sentenced to 20 years (6 for sexual abuse, 14 for rape) for abusing an 11-year-old boy in his parish in 2002–2003. In August 2022 a civil court ordered the archbishop and two church entities to pay about US$100,000 in damages.
cases.cite: El Observador (Costa Rica), 30 March 2022; AP via Voz de América, 24 Aug 2022

cases.n: Puerto Rico — Arecibo priests defrocked; island-wide probe
cases.victims_note: six priests expelled; at least 11 more under investigation
cases.who: Diocese of Arecibo; at least four Puerto Rican dioceses
cases.cover: Prosecutor Yolanda Pitino said the diocese's information was insufficient and it had not answered requests for more; Justice Secretary César Miranda warned he might charge church officials suspected of withholding information.
cases.d: In early 2014, after reports in El Nuevo Día, Bishop Daniel Fernández disclosed that since 2011 he had expelled six priests accused of sexual abuse in the Arecibo diocese. Local prosecutors said at least 11 other priests on the island were under investigation, and the Justice Secretary said at least four dioceses were being investigated. U.S. Homeland Security Investigations requested information.
cases.cite: Associated Press via Fox News, 2014

cases.n: Uruguay — Episcopal Conference apology
cases.who: Episcopal Conference of Uruguay
cases.cover: The abuses, about 20 years earlier, went unpunished because the statute of limitations had expired.
cases.d: In April 2016 Uruguay's bishops apologised, expressing 'pain and shame', after receiving reports the previous year of three people abused by priests as teenagers. Auxiliary Bishop Milton Troccoli said one priest left the priesthood and another was removed after an investigation; criminal charges were time-barred.
cases.cite: Associated Press via Fox News, April 2016

cases.n: Honduras — Fr Joseph Maurizio, orphanage trips
cases.who: Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown, Pennsylvania (Somerset County parish); orphanage in El Progreso
cases.d: A Pennsylvania priest was found guilty by a U.S. federal jury in September 2015 on three of four counts of sexually abusing minors during trips to an orphanage in El Progreso, Honduras, between 2004 and 2009. He was also convicted of possessing child abuse material and of illegally transferring money to a charity to fund the trips.
cases.cite: La Prensa (Honduras), 23 Sept 2015

cases.n: El Salvador — Guatemalan priest arrested in San Salvador
cases.who: Archdiocese of San Salvador
cases.d: On 13 April 2019 Salvadoran police arrested Guatemalan priest José Venancio Boror Uz, 62, outside his parish in San Salvador; prosecutors charged him with sexual assault of a six-year-old girl and he was held in pre-trial detention. Archbishop José Luis Escobar announced the charge at Mass and apologised to the victim's family.
cases.cite: Emisoras Unidas (Guatemala), 16 April 2019, citing AFP and PNC El Salvador

cases.n: Japan — Bishops' Conference survey: 16 cases
cases.who: Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan (16 dioceses)
cases.cover: Eight accused clerics were transferred; some punished clerics kept working or moved to another diocese; five remained priests. Only one denied case was examined by a third-party panel.
cases.d: The Catholic Bishops' Conference of Japan began a survey of all 16 dioceses in May 2019 and published it on 7 April 2020. It found 16 cases of sexual abuse of minors from the 1950s to the 2010s, called 'the tip of the iceberg'. Most victims took 10 to 30 years to report, some 50 to 70 years. Of the accused, seven were Japanese priests and eight religious or missionaries, seven of them foreign. Earlier internal surveys (2002, 2012) had found two and five cases.
cases.cite: Asahi Shimbun, 16 April 2020; CNA / Catholic World Report, 3 April 2020

cases.n: Sri Lanka — temple chief monk jailed for abusing boy brought for ordination
cases.who: Sri Sambuddha Walukarama Temple (Theravada Buddhist)
cases.d: The Anuradhapura Special High Court for Child Crimes convicted the 65-year-old chief incumbent of a temple in Thalakolawawa on three charges of sexually abusing a 14-year-old boy brought to the temple for ordination in May 2022. He received three 10-year terms, ordered to run concurrently (10 years effective) and Rs 500,000 compensation. The Attorney General's Department prosecuted after a Thambuttegama Police investigation.
cases.cite: Tamil Guardian, citing AsianMirror, 2026

cases.n: Sri Lanka — senior Anuradhapura monk arrested (2026)
cases.who: Malwathu Chapter (Theravada Buddhist)
cases.d: In 2026 police arrested a senior Buddhist monk, a former chief prelate (Atamasthanadhipathi) of Anuradhapura, over allegations of sexually abusing an underage girl. The Malwathu Chapter suspended him from religious duties pending the case; he denies the allegations. Rights groups cited delays and accountability problems in cases involving senior monks.
cases.cite: Tamil Guardian, 2026; The Week / PTI, 9 May 2026

cases.n: Nigeria — Anglican priest jailed in Ekiti for defiling a five-year-old
cases.who: Anglican Church (Church of Nigeria)
cases.d: On 5 August 2019 an Ado-Ekiti High Court sentenced Anglican priest Gabriel Asateru, 53, to five years in prison and a N50,000 fine under the Ekiti State Child Rights Law for defiling a five-year-old girl on or about 23 December 2016 while visiting her parents in Ifisin-Ekiti.
cases.cite: News Agency of Nigeria via The Nigeria Lawyer; ThisDay, 6 Aug 2019

cases.n: Nigeria — Winners Chapel pastor given life for raping a minor (Ekiti)
cases.who: Living Faith Church (Winners Chapel), Omuo-Ekiti
cases.d: The Ekiti State High Court in Ado-Ekiti sentenced Enoch Gbinyiam, a pastor of Winners Chapel in Omuo-Ekiti, to life imprisonment for raping the daughter of a church member who visited the vicarage to help with chores, after sedating her drink. The conviction was under the state's Gender Based Violence (Prohibition) Law, 2019.
cases.cite: Ripples Nigeria

cases.n: IICSA — Child protection in religious organisations and settings (2021)
cases.who: 38 religious organisations in England and Wales, including churches, mosques, synagogues, temples and out-of-school faith settings
cases.cover: The Inquiry found victim-blaming, discouraging external reporting and putting reputation above victims; some organisations serving large congregations had no child protection policy at all.
cases.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse published its report on 2 September 2021 after taking evidence from 38 religious organisations. It found child sexual abuse in most major UK religions and 'shocking failings' in prevention and response. An estimated 250,000 children attend faith-based supplementary or out-of-school settings, which need not register with any state body and have no child-protection oversight. Among cases heard, a mosque Qur'an teacher who abused four children aged about nine was convicted in 2017 and jailed for 13 years. It recommended that every religious organisation have a child protection policy and that the law on full-time education be changed so unregistered schools come under Ofsted.
cases.cite: IICSA, 'Child protection in religious organisations and settings' investigation report, 2 September 2021

cases.n: Methodist Church (Britain) — Past Cases Review
cases.victims_note: 1,885 cases of sexual, physical, emotional and domestic abuse or neglect since 1950, involving children, young people and adults; not all were child sexual abuse
cases.who: Methodist Church in Britain
cases.cover: The church said abuse by some Methodists had been ignored or not listened to; it issued an 'unreserved apology'.
cases.d: Published on 28 May 2015 after three years of research, the Methodist Church's Past Cases Review found 1,885 cases of sexual, physical, emotional and domestic abuse or neglect going back to 1950. In 26% of cases church ministers or lay employees were identified as the alleged perpetrators. Six police investigations were ongoing. General Secretary Martyn Atkins made an unreserved apology.
cases.cite: Methodist Church Past Cases Review, May 2015, as reported by AP (Fox News) and Toronto Star, 28 May 2015

cases.n: Bob Jones University — GRACE report
cases.victims_note: 50 people who self-identified as victims of sexual abuse were interviewed; many had suffered child sexual abuse before arriving
cases.who: Bob Jones University (independent fundamentalist Christian)
cases.cover: Several victims said campus counselors did not report their abuse to legal authorities; counseling blamed victims and treated all 'sexual sin' as equal. The university fired and then rehired GRACE during the investigation.
cases.d: Bob Jones University hired GRACE (Godly Response to Abuse in the Christian Environment) in November 2012 to review its handling of sexual abuse. GRACE's roughly 300-page report, released 11 December 2014, found the school responded to abuse claims with ignorance of state reporting law, little trauma training and a culture that blamed victims; some counselors encouraged victims to repent. The review was prompted in part by a board member's handling of a 1997 case in which a minor girl raped by a church deacon in New Hampshire was made to confess before the congregation. The university president apologised.
cases.cite: GRACE, Final Report on Bob Jones University, 11 Dec 2014, as reported by RNS (Christian Century) and The American Prospect, Dec 2014

cases.n: Royal Commission Case Study 36 — Church of England Boys' Society
cases.place: Tasmania, Adelaide, Brisbane and Sydney dioceses
cases.who: Church of England Boys' Society (now Anglican Boys' Society / Boys' Ministry Australia); Anglican dioceses of Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Tasmania
cases.cover: Allegations were not reported to police at all or not in time; a parish priest told one victim to 'let sleeping dogs lie'. The report found Peter Hollingworth, former Archbishop of Brisbane and later Governor-General, made 'a serious error of judgment' in letting an accused priest continue in ministry.
cases.d: The Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse reported in February 2017 that the CEBS youth group gave paedophiles easy access to boys from the 1970s to the 1990s, with abuse on camps, sailing and fishing trips and overnight stays at rectories. It found 'networks of sexual perpetrators at CEBS who had knowledge of each other's sexual offending against boys and in some instances facilitated' it; several associated men were later convicted. It found a focus on protecting the reputation of the church, dioceses, CEBS and clergy.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 36, Feb 2017, as reported by Illawarra Mercury (Fairfax), 13 Feb 2017

cases.n: Royal Commission Case Study 42 — Anglican Diocese of Newcastle
cases.victims_note: 19 male victims in Fr James Brown's 2011 convictions alone
cases.who: Anglican Diocese of Newcastle (Bishops Alfred Holland 1978–92, Roger Herft 1993–2005)
cases.cover: Found a 'do nothing' approach under Bishop Holland and a 'weak and ineffectual' response under Bishop Herft; complainants were treated as liars and sometimes threatened with legal action; abusive relationships were misrepresented as consensual; dioceses receiving moved clergy were not warned; diocesan lawyers acted for accused priests. Former dean Graeme Lawrence was defrocked.
cases.d: The Royal Commission's report, released on 7 December 2017 after hearings in August and November 2016, found systemic issues let a group of perpetrators operate in the diocese for at least 30 years. Fr Peter Rushton died in 2007 never charged, though the diocese acknowledges he was a child sex offender. Fr James Brown pleaded guilty in 2011 to 27 child sexual abuse charges relating to 19 boys and was jailed for up to 20 years. Bishop Herft resigned as Archbishop of Perth in 2016. Later bishops Brian Farran and Greg Thompson acted against alleged perpetrators and faced backlash.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 42, 7 Dec 2017, as reported by Newcastle Herald and AAP

cases.n: Nigeria — Kaduna 'Islamic school' raid frees 300+ boys and men
cases.victims_note: more than 300 boys and men, some as young as five; sexual abuse reported by local media, not confirmed by Reuters
cases.who: Imam Ahmad Bun Hambal Centre for Islamic Studies (purported Islamic school / rehabilitation centre)
cases.d: On 26 September 2019 Kaduna police raided a building signed as an Islamic studies centre and freed more than 300 boys and men, many chained and with whip scars. Some had been brought from Burkina Faso, Mali and Ghana; families said they were denied access. Seven people claiming to be teachers were arrested. Local media reported captives were tortured, starved and sexually abused. The raid led to further rescues from similar 'torture houses' in northern Nigeria.
cases.cite: Reuters via Africanews, 27 Sept 2019

cases.n: Thailand — 'Jet-set monk' Wirapol Sukphol convicted of abducting and raping a girl
cases.who: Wat Pa Khantitham forest monastery (Theravada Buddhist)
cases.cover: He fled to the United States after a 2013 video exposed his lifestyle and was extradited back in July 2017.
cases.d: Former abbot Wirapol Sukphol was convicted by Bangkok's Criminal Court in October 2018 of abducting a 13-year-old girl from her parents and sexually abusing her in 2000 and 2001; DNA matched him to a child the girl bore. He received 16 years, added to a 114-year term for fraud and money laundering imposed in August 2018. The court cited his flight to the U.S. as aggravating.
cases.cite: Asia Times, Oct 2018

cases.n: Thailand — Buriram abbot confessed to raping a girl from age 13
cases.who: Wat Muang Doo (Theravada Buddhist); Buriram Provincial Office of Buddhism
cases.cover: After confessing and being charged, the abbot paid the poor family 150,000 baht to withdraw the case and then reportedly fled to another province rather than be defrocked.
cases.d: The 52-year-old abbot, who led school meditation sessions, took a 13-year-old girl from her school's nurse's office to his temple in 2015, drugged and raped her, and kept abusing her for five years under threat of releasing recordings. The abuse came to light in August 2019 when she was five months pregnant. He confessed and was charged with rape. The Provincial Office of Buddhism said he must be defrocked.
cases.cite: Khaosod English, 3 Sept 2019

cases.n: Thailand — Chiang Dao monks arrested for procuring a boy for an abbot
cases.who: Temple in Chiang Dao (Theravada Buddhist)
cases.d: On 19 June 2013 Chiang Mai police arrested two young monks, aged 20 and 23, accused of repeatedly taking a 14-year-old boy to a temple abbot for sexual services since February. Police said the two faced up to 15 years in jail; the abbot had not yet been arrested pending a warrant.
cases.cite: Chiang Mai CityNews, 20 June 2013, citing AFP

flows.n: Tehuacán → Los Angeles → Mexico: Fr Nicolás Aguilar Rivera
flows.d: A Mexican priest was presented to the Los Angeles archdiocese by his bishop in January 1987; within a year 26 children were reported abused, and he fled back to Mexico before arrest on 19 felony counts.

flows.n: Minnesota → India: Fr Joseph Jeyapaul (returned by extradition 2014)
flows.d: Removed from ministry in Minnesota in 2005, he returned to India and continued as a priest; charged in 2006, he was arrested in Erode in 2012 and extradited back in 2014.
Indicted in Arizona in 2003, the Salvatorian priest went to Italy and evaded a confirmed extradition until his arrest in Rome in May 2019.
Rivoire left the Arctic for France in January 1993; Canadian warrants (1998, 2022) went unexecuted and France refused extradition. He died in France in 2024.

flows.n: Scranton (USA) → Ciudad del Este (Paraguay): Fr Carlos Urrutigoity
flows.d: After 2002 accusations in Scranton, the priest and his group moved to Ciudad del Este, where he became vicar general in 2014; he was moved to Mendoza, Argentina in 2015.

flows.n: Costa Rica → Mexico: Fr Mauricio Víquez (flight, extradited 2021)
flows.to: San Nicolás de los Garza, Nuevo León, Mexico
flows.d: The priest fled in 2018 via Panama to Mexico, where he was caught and extradited in 2021; he was sentenced to 20 years in 2022.
flows.cite: AP via Voz de América, 24 Aug 2022

flows.n: Pennsylvania → El Progreso, Honduras: Fr Joseph Maurizio
flows.d: A Pennsylvania priest abused minors on charity trips to a Honduran orphanage between 2004 and 2009, funded partly through illegal money transfers; convicted 2015.

flows.n: Burkina Faso / Mali / Ghana → Kaduna: children held in purported Islamic school
flows.d: Police said some of the 300+ captives freed in the 2019 Kaduna raid had been brought from Burkina Faso, Mali and Ghana.

flows.n: Sisaket → United States: 'jet-set monk' Wirapol (fugitive, extradited 2017)
flows.d: The former abbot fled to the U.S. after 2013 exposure and was extradited to Thailand in July 2017, then convicted of abducting and raping a girl.

notes: South Korea: the Feb 2018 CBCK apology concerned an attempted rape of an adult woman (South Sudan mission, 2011), not a minor, so it was not recorded as a child case. Uruguay: an ACI Prensa piece headlined '40 denunciados por abusos en 70 años' could not be read (page body not loaded), so its figures are not used.
